def odd_Days(N):
    """Write a python function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.

    Return the number of odd days in ``N`` years, counting from year 1.

    An ordinary year has 1 odd day (365 == 52 * 7 + 1) and a leap year
    has 2 odd days (366 == 52 * 7 + 2), so the result is the total
    modulo 7. Leap years use the Gregorian rule: a year is a leap year
    if it is divisible by 4, except century years, which are leap years
    only if divisible by 400. For example, 100 years contain 24 leap
    years, giving (100 + 24) % 7 == 5 odd days.
    """
    leap_years = N // 4 - N // 100 + N // 400
    return (N + leap_years) % 7

    assert solution.odd_Days(2) == 2

def test_odd_days_leap_years():
    # Years 1-4: three ordinary years and one leap year.
    assert solution.odd_Days(4) == 5
    assert solution.odd_Days(5) == 6
    # The total reaches a whole number of weeks after 6 years.
    assert solution.odd_Days(6) == 0
    assert solution.odd_Days(7) == 1
    assert solution.odd_Days(10) == 5


def test_odd_days_century_years():
    # 100 is not a leap year, but 400 is.
    assert solution.odd_Days(99) == 4
    assert solution.odd_Days(100) == 5

    assert solution.odd_Days(300) == 1
